findings.title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed/terminated
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive and join the code guards cleanup with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). Processes are created with self.mp_context.Process where mp_context is multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), whose class is SpawnProcess (a BaseProcess sibling of the default ForkProcess exposed as multiprocessing.Process). The isinstance check is therefore False for real flusher processes, so process.kill() on hang/crash and process.terminate() in join() never run. Consequence: hung processes are not reaped while a replacement is started (duplicate flushing of the same shards, fd/process leaks), and join() can wait/hang instead of terminating children.

findings.title: Invalid flusher-process count can silently disable flushing
findings.body: self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) treats 0 as unset, and self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) accepts negative values. The --flusher-processes CLI option has no validation, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes shard-count instead of 0, and a negative value yields range(negative) == empty, i.e. zero entries in process_to_shards_map and zero flusher processes. With zero processes nothing ever calls flush_segments/done_flush_segments, so segments accumulate in Redis forever and are never produced to buffered-segments.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name shards vs shard
findings.body: Produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} but the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Consumers of spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce grouped by shard will see a new tag key after this change, breaking existing dashboards/alerts and splitting series. The tag key should be shard in both places.
